text: Malaysia's Industrial Court ruled in 2020 and again in June 2021 in favour of migrant workers in pay cases against Goodyear Malaysia, the local operation of The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co, ordering it to pay back wages to 109 migrant workers and comply with its collective agreement, after finding the workers from Nepal, Myanmar and India had been denied the shift allowances, bonuses and pay rises given to Malaysian staff. Malaysia's labour department said it had charged and fined Goodyear in 2020 over excessive hours and wrongful salary deductions of foreign employees; payslips filed in court showed migrants working up to 229 hours of overtime a month against a legal limit of 104, and workers and officials described withheld passports and threats.
short: A Malaysian court ordered Goodyear to repay migrant workers denied locals' benefits, and the labour department fined it over hours and wage deductions (2020-21).

source.name: The Straits Times (Reuters): US tyre maker Goodyear accused of labour abuses in Malaysia
source.quote: The court ruled in favour of the foreign workers in two of the cases last year, saying they were entitled to the same rights as Malaysian employees
source.note: Also in the article: Malaysia's labour department confirmed it had fined Goodyear RM41,500 in 2020 for overworking and underpaying foreign employees, and had charged it over nine labour-law violations.
